title: A celebration beyond its perfect appearance
meaning: Shared joy becomes freer when abandoning false conditions leaves you unbound by making the celebration even richer.
text: A pleasant evening can be obstructed by a rule treated as its foundation. The Tower in the physical position of Svadhisthana describes decisively abandoning conditions that fail. The Empress in energy leans towards immediately adding beauty and treats so the celebration will still feel complete. The Sun in emotions allows direct enjoyment without proving outward perfection. Simple joy may appear after releasing the strict picture. It still needs room, beyond turning new freedom into another abundant programme for both people.

Suppose you imagined a formal dinner at home, then notice that table settings receive constant corrections while conversation scarcely happens. **Releasing extra conditions can restore pleasure in the meeting itself.** You can remove some decorations, sit and taste what is ready. Mismatched plates become a shared joke instead of a fault. Attention and flavour give the evening living content without immediately surpassing the original design before both may enjoy being close.

The difficulty is believing that a broken programme demands even more. You prepare another dish, change music and await brighter enthusiasm. A false condition survives: pleasure must equal the scale of effort. Immediate feeling follows no such measure. It may be quiet or brief and remain real. A dismantled scheme frees leisure when both may enjoy what is available without continually intensifying impressions or confirming the success of every preparation.
